what_it_does: A processor core executes one instruction at a time in strict order ('in-order' execution), which is simple and energy-efficient but slow. A dual-issue core can execute two instructions simultaneously, nearly doubling throughput — but traditionally requires extra hardware that increases chip area and energy consumption. Modern programs mix two flavors of instructions: integer operations (comparisons, additions on whole numbers) and floating-point operations (arithmetic on decimal numbers), handled by separate internal units. This paper proposes a way to pair those two kinds of units together so they fire in tandem with minimal extra circuitry, effectively getting dual-issue speedups on a low-power processor design built around the open RISC-V instruction set. New instruction-set extensions are introduced to signal which integer and floating-point instructions can safely execute together.
